questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body moving with velocity v collides head on and elastically with an identical body at rest. After the collision:
options: The first body rebounds with v
questions.explanation: In a one dimensional elastic collision of equal masses, momentum and kinetic energy are both conserved only if the velocities are exchanged, so the first stops and the second moves off with v.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The statement that the energy radiated per unit area per unit time by a black body is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature is known as:
questions.explanation: E = σT⁴ is the Stefan-Boltzmann law. Wien's law instead relates the wavelength of maximum emission to temperature.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 10: Thermal Properties of Matter

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The self-inductance of a coil does NOT depend on:
questions.explanation: L = μ₀μᵣN²A/l is fixed by geometry and the core, not by the current. The current only decides the flux and the induced emf.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A reaction for which ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive will be:
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. With ΔH negative and -TΔS also negative, ΔG stays negative at every temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ and [NiCl₄]²⁻ is correct?
options: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is square planar and diamagnetic; [NiCl₄]²⁻ is tetrahedral and paramagnetic
Both are square planar and diamagnetic
[Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is tetrahedral and paramagnetic; [NiCl₄]²⁻ is square planar
questions.explanation: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand and pairs the 3d electrons, giving dsp² square planar geometry with no unpaired electrons. Weak field Cl⁻ leaves two unpaired electrons in sp³ tetrahedral geometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The carbylamine reaction, which gives a foul smelling isocyanide, is a laboratory test for:
questions.explanation: Only primary amines heated with chloroform and alcoholic KOH give isocyanides; secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is NOT bounded by a double membrane?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are single membrane bound vesicles budded off from the Golgi apparatus, while mitochondria, plastids and the nucleus all have two membranes.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Red-green colour blindness in humans is inherited as:
questions.explanation: The gene lies on the X chromosome, so a male with a single defective X is affected, while a female must inherit the allele from both parents.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: HIV multiplies in and progressively destroys which cells of the immune system?
questions.explanation: Loss of helper T cells cripples the whole immune response, which is why AIDS patients suffer repeated opportunistic infections.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Red muscle fibres differ from white muscle fibres in having:
options: Plenty of myoglobin and numerous mitochondria
questions.explanation: Red fibres are rich in myoglobin and mitochondria, so they respire aerobically and resist fatigue; white fibres rely on anaerobic respiration and tire quickly.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement
